title: Fatal Fury Special
subtitle: A larger gathering in South Town
summary: Fatal Fury Special is SNK's expanded revision of Fatal Fury 2, released in Japanese arcades on 16 September 1993.
body: Fatal Fury Special is SNK's expanded revision of Fatal Fury 2, released in Japanese arcades on 16 September 1993. Returning fighters and newly playable bosses bring the roster to fifteen, giving players more ways into the series' contest. The fighting takes place across two lines, allowing movement into and out of an opponent's immediate plane. Familiar backgrounds and characters gain another life through the faster pace and revised systems, turning a refinement of an existing game into a substantial gathering of the cast.

A new combo system lets successful attacks connect into further blows, increasing the value of recognizing an opening. Changes to line attacks provide more ways to strike an opponent positioned on the other plane. The movement of a fight therefore concerns both ordinary distance and the relationship between the two lines. Choosing a returning character or one of the former bosses gives those systems another set of strengths to work with. The revision adjusts the rhythm of individual exchanges while preserving the series' distinctive layered battlefield.

Tung Fu Rue, Duck King and Geese Howard return from the first Fatal Fury, while Billy Kane, Axel Hawk, Laurence Blood and Wolfgang Krauser become playable. A hidden encounter brings Art of Fighting's Ryo Sakazaki into a Dream Match after an exceptional single-player run. That crossover helped inspire The King of Fighters. Fatal Fury Special reached AES in December 1993 before further ports followed. Its lasting importance lies partly in that expanded encounter: SNK's separate fighting worlds could share a contest without losing their recognizable characters.
